title: ARTIC SARS-CoV-2 Sequencing Protocol v4
author: Josh Quick
materials: 0 µL Set-up the following program on the thermal cycler: Step Temperature Time Cycles Heat Activation 98 °C 00:00:30 1 Denaturation 98 °C 00:00:15 25-35 Annealing 65 °C 00:05:00 25-35 Hold 4 °C Indefinite 1 Cycle number should be 25 for Ct 18-21 up to a maximum of 35 cycles for Ct 35. Thermocycler calibration can vary instrument to instrument. If you see amplicon 64 dropout then decrease the annealing/extension temperature to 63 °C . Denaturation temperature of 95 °C can also be used and may slightly increase PCR yields.

steps.title: Prepare RNA samples and dilutions
steps.instruction: Thaw 11–95 clinical RNA samples (plus one nuclease‑free water negative control) on ice, vortex briefly if frozen and pulse‑spin. Keep all samples on ice. Record each sample’s Ct value. If Ct 12–15 dilute the sample 1:100 in water; if Ct 15–18 dilute 1:10 in water; samples with Ct 18–35 are used undiluted. If processing >23 samples, use the EXP‑NBD196 expansion kit; if <11 samples, increase downstream DNA volumes as described in the native‑barcoding section. Include a positive control (synthetic RNA or high‑titre clinical sample) if desired.

steps.title: Prepare primer pools (if needed)
steps.instruction: If not using the IDT ARTIC nCoV‑2019 V5.3.2 Panel (100 µM), fully resuspend each lyophilised oligo in 1× TE to 100 µM, vortex thoroughly and spin down. Dilute each 100 µM pool 1:10 with molecular‑grade water to make 10 µM primer stocks. Primers are used at a final 15 nM per primer; for V3 pools (110 primers in pool 1, 108 in pool 2) this equals ~4 µL of the 10 µM pool per 25 µL PCR reaction. Prepare multiple 100 µL aliquots of the 10 µM stocks and freeze. Sort odd‑region primers into one rack, add 5 µL of each odd‑region primer to a 1.5 mL tube labelled “Pool 1 (100 µM)”; repeat for even‑region primers in “Pool 2 (100 µM)”. Perform all primer dilution and pooling in the mastermix cabinet cleaned with decontamination wipes and UV‑sterilised before and after use.

steps.title: Assemble PCR mastermix in clean cabinet
steps.instruction: In the mastermix cabinet (cleaned with decontamination wipes and UV‑sterilised before and after), combine the ARTIC PCR kit components (or Q5 Hot Start High‑Fidelity 2× Master Mix as an alternative) in PCR strip‑tubes or a plate. Gently mix by pipetting and pulse‑spin to collect liquid. Half‑scale reactions (2.5 µL per downstream step) may be prepared to save costs.

steps.title: Add cDNA to PCR reactions
steps.instruction: In the extraction/sample‑addition cabinet (cleaned and UV‑sterilised), add 2.5 µL of each cDNA sample to the corresponding PCR reaction and gently mix by pipetting, then pulse‑spin. Up to 5 µL cDNA may replace nuclease‑free water to improve amplification of low‑titre samples; using 5 µL requires a 20 µL total reaction volume and may increase inhibition, so use cautiously.

steps.title: Thermocycle PCR reactions
steps.instruction: Place the PCR strip‑tubes/plate in a thermocycler and run: 25 °C for 2 min, 55 °C for 10 min, 95 °C for 1 min, then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Optional: Verify PCR product concentration
steps.instruction: If desired, measure DNA concentration of a subset of PCR products with a fluorometer (Qubit or Quantus). Typical yields are 80–100 ng/µL; if a sample is <50 ng/µL, double the amount of that product in the next step. This check is optional for large batches.

steps.title: Label and pool PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Label each strip‑tube/plate. Combine 10 µL of each PCR product into a single pool per sample. The post‑clean‑up concentration is usually ~100 ng/µL, allowing pooling without prior quantification. If highly even barcode representation is required, perform a clean‑up and normalize each amplicon to 10 ng/µL before pooling. Perform pooling in the post‑PCR cabinet (cleaned and UV‑sterilised).

steps.title: Perform one‑pot native barcoding
steps.instruction: Barcode the pooled amplicons using the one‑pot native barcoding protocol (v4, LoCost) as described by Josh Quick.

steps.title: Quantify barcoded amplicons (~30 ng total)
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of the barcoded amplicon pool with a fluorometer (Qubit or Quatus). Ensure you have approximately 30 ng total DNA at this stage to achieve maximum run yield.

steps.title: Ligate Native Adapter using SFB
steps.instruction: Set up the Native Adapter (NA) ligation according to the current Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) kit protocol, using Short Fragment Buffer (SFB) for the clean‑up step.

steps.title: Quantify final library (~15 ng) and store
steps.instruction: Quantify the ligated library with a fluorometer (Qubit or Quatus). Aim for 15 ng of final library (required for optimal loading of short amplicons). Store the library in 10 mM Tris, pH 8, at 4 °C for up to one week if not proceeding immediately to sequencing.

steps.title: Prime and load flowcell with library
steps.instruction: Prime the MinION flowcell and load 15 ng of the sequencing library following the ONT protocol for the kit you purchased. Loading >15 ng may cause speed drops; loading <15 ng may yield <20 M reads.

steps.title: Start MinKNOW run with live basecalling
steps.instruction: Plug the MinION into the computer (with the flowcell already loaded) and wait for detection. In MinKNOW, name the run, select the appropriate kit(s), enable ‘barcode both ends’, enable ‘trim barcodes’, and select ‘live basecalling’ (recommended) with the High‑Accuracy mode. Ensure double‑ended barcoding is turned on in the basecalling settings.
